subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should literal `openai` session route state be claimed by the Codex doctor owner, by a separate OpenAI doctor owner, or by a shared core doctor owner?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but OpenClaw policy keeps owner-specific provider behavior in the owning plugin and treats OpenAI Codex as folded into `openai`, so automation should not choose the provider ownership contract on its own.

options.title: Codex owns OpenAI Codex route cleanup
options.body: Add `openai` and matching auth prefixes to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers want Codex to own canonical OpenAI session pins that route through the native Codex harness.

options.title: OpenAI plugin owns literal openai
options.body: Add a lightweight OpenAI doctor contract that owns `openai` route-state cleanup while keeping Codex responsible only for legacy Codex ids and runtime pins.

options.title: Core owns shared OpenAI route cleanup
options.body: Move literal `openai` stale-session cleanup into a core doctor owner when maintainers want the repair independent of bundled provider plugin availability.

recommendation.title: Codex owns OpenAI Codex route cleanup
recommendation.body: Add `openai` and matching auth prefixes to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers want Codex to own canonical OpenAI session pins that route through the native Codex harness.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the prior generic doctor route-state repair and Codex providerless session repair, making him the strongest history-backed owner for this boundary decision.
